research_mode: official MHCLG electrical-safety guidance only; regulatory scope, inspection, EICR classification and enforcement methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical-safety guidance scope
verified_claims: The guidance applies in England and covers private and social rented sectors after the 2025 extension.
limitations: Regulatory scope does not establish the condition of any named property.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Five-year electrical-installation inspection duty
verified_claims: Landlords must have electrical installations inspected and tested by a qualified person at least every five years.
limitations: The interval does not prove that an installation remained safe between inspections.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical report distribution duty
verified_claims: Landlords must obtain a report and provide it to tenants and to the local council when requested.
limitations: A report's existence is not evidence that all remedial work has been completed.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential-tenancy coverage gate
verified_claims: The regulations generally apply where a tenant occupies the premises as their only or main residence and pays rent.
limitations: Coverage depends on the legal occupancy arrangement and listed exceptions.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical-regulation tenancy exclusions
verified_claims: The guidance lists exclusions including certain shared accommodation, long leases, student halls, hostels, care settings and mobile homes.
limitations: An exclusion category must not be inferred without tenancy-specific evidence.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: BS 7671 electrical-safety standard
verified_claims: Electrical safety standards are set out in British Standard 7671, the 18th Edition Wiring Regulations.
limitations: Referencing BS 7671 does not prove compliance by a specific installation.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Permanently connected electrical-equipment scope
verified_claims: Electrical installations include permanently connected equipment and circuits for specialist equipment such as solar PV and battery storage.
limitations: Inclusion in scope does not identify the equipment present at a parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical inspection hazard family
verified_claims: Inspection considers overload, electric-shock risk, fire hazards, defective work and missing earthing or bonding.
limitations: The hazard checklist is not a finding that any named property has those defects.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: EICR result and next-inspection date
verified_claims: The inspection report gives the results and sets a date for the next inspection and test.
limitations: The next date must be read from the actual report and cannot be assumed from publication guidance.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical C1 classification
verified_claims: Code C1 means danger is present and there is a risk of injury.
limitations: A C1 definition is not evidence that a C1 defect exists at a named property.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical C2 classification
limitations: A C2 definition cannot be converted into a parcel-level probability without an inspection report.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical C3 classification
verified_claims: Code C3 means improvement is recommended and does not by itself require remedial work for a satisfactory report.
limitations: C3 should not be represented as either confirmed danger or confirmed absence of risk.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical further-investigation classification
verified_claims: FI means further investigation is required without delay.
limitations: FI does not state the final defect or outcome of that investigation.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Social-landlord electrical-equipment check
verified_claims: Social landlords must have electrical equipment they provide checked by a qualified person at least every five years.
limitations: The duty applies to landlord-provided equipment and does not establish equipment condition.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Electrical-safety financial-penalty ceiling
verified_claims: Local councils may impose a financial penalty of up to £40,000 for specified breaches.
limitations: A statutory ceiling is not evidence that a landlord has breached the regulations or received a penalty.
